notes.text: **[Hosea 14:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Hosea.14.2)** — שׁוּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל עַד ה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ כִּי כָשַׁלְתָּ בַּעֲוֺנֶךָ — Return, Israel, to Hashem your God, for you have stumbled in your iniquity. The closing section of the Vayetzei haftarah; Rav Tzadok asks why a call to teshuvah is read with this parashah. *Mafteach: found*

**[Hosea 12:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Hosea.12.13)** — וַיִּבְרַח יַעֲקֹב שְׂדֵה אֲרָם וַיַּעֲבֹד יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאִשָּׁה וּבְאִשָּׁה שָׁמָר — Yaakov fled to the field of Aram; Israel served for a wife, and for a wife he kept [sheep]. The haftarah opens here, so on the simple level it matches the parashah's story; Rav Tzadok goes on to show that the whole parashah also points to its end, "Return, O Israel." *Mafteach: found*
**[Genesis 28:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.28.10)** — וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שָׁבַע וַיֵּלֶךְ חָרָנָה — Yaakov went out from Be'er Sheva and went to Charan. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 147a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.1.3-4)** (Vayetzei) — רִבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אָמַר, נָפִיק מִכְּלָלָא דְאַרְעָא דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, דִּכְתִיב וַיֵּצֵא יַעֲקֹב מִבְּאֵר שָׁבַע. וְאֲזַל לִרְשׁוּ אָחֳרָא, דִּכְתִיב וַיֵּלֶךְ חָרָנָה — R. Shimon: he went out from the domain of the Land of Israel, and went into another domain. Rav Tzadok quotes R. Shimon word for word. The passage opens the Zohar on Vayetzei; its first paragraph starts on 146b, but R. Shimon's words stand on 147a. *Mafteach: wrong address (index: Zohar I 146a; correct: Zohar I 147a)*

**[Zohar I 147a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.1.3-4)** (Vayetzei) and **[Bereshit Rabbah 70:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.70.10)** — both read the parashah as the exile. The Zohar: רבי יוסי מוקי האי קרא בגלותא ... וביומי דגלותא, נטיל מהאי באר שבע, ואזיל לגבי חרנה, דכתיב וילך חרנה, כלומר חרון אף — R. Yose sets the verse in the exile: in the days of exile he leaves Be'er Sheva for Charan, that is, the burning anger. The Midrash: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא פָּתַר קְרָיָא בַּגָּלוּת — R. Yose bar Chanina read the passage as speaking of the exile. Rav Tzadok quotes the Midrash below ([1.18]–[1.24]). *Mafteach: missing*

**[Genesis 29:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.29.2)** — וַיַּרְא וְהִנֵּה בְאֵר בַּשָּׂדֶה וְהִנֵּה שָׁם שְׁלֹשָׁה עֶדְרֵי צֹאן רֹבְצִים עָלֶיהָ — He looked, and behold, a well in the field, and three flocks of sheep lying beside it. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Vayetzei 6](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Vayetzei_6) (Rav Tzadok) — explains the same verse through the Zohar (151b, Sitrei Torah): באר דרגא דאדון כל הארץ בשדה חקל תפוחין קדישין, the well is Malchut, the field of holy apples, and Yaakov is the river that waters it. That is why the meeting at the well is where Knesset Yisrael is built. It adds that "well" appears seven times with Yaakov in this parashah, a full number. *checked*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 70:10](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.70.10)** — מֵחָרָן אֲנָחְנוּ, מֵחֲרוֹנוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא אָנוּ בּוֹרְחִים ... הַיְדַעְתֶּם אֶת לָבָן בֶּן נָחוֹר, הַיְדַעְתֶּם אֶת מִי שֶׁהוּא עָתִיד לְלַבֵּן עֲוֹנוֹתֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁלֶג — "From Charan": from the wrath of the Holy One we are fleeing. "Do you know Lavan?": do you know the One who will in the future whiten your sins like snow. R. Yose bar Chanina reads Yaakov's talk with the shepherds as a dialogue with Israel in exile. Rav Tzadok builds the whole os on the second half: the exile leads to the whitening of sin. *Mafteach: found*

**[Genesis 29:4–5](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.29.4-5)** — וַיֹּאמְרוּ מֵחָרָן אֲנָחְנוּ ... וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם הַיְדַעְתֶּם אֶת לָבָן בֶּן נָחוֹר וַיֹּאמְרוּ יָדָעְנוּ — They said, "We are from Charan." He said to them, "Do you know Lavan son of Nachor?" They said, "We know him." The two verses the Midrash expounds. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Recanati on the Torah, Vayetzei 13](https://www.sefaria.org/Recanati_on_the_Torah,_Vayetzei.13)** (Kabbalah) — Recanati also uses this Midrash to read Lavan, despite his wickedness, as a name for a supernal attribute (for him, Chesed): Yaakov waters "Lavan's sheep" with waters of teshuvah and mercy. Rav Tzadok reads the name the same way, as Levanon that whitens sin.
סמך לזה מצאתי לרז"ל בבראשית רבה אמרו שם ויאמר להם הידעתם את לבן בן נחור הידעתם את מי שהוא עתיד ללבן עונותיכם כשלג

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Sefat Emet, Genesis, Vayetzei 20](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefat_Emet,_Genesis,_Vayetzei.20)** (Chassidus) — the Sefat Emet reads the same Midrash ("from Charan... who will whiten") as Yaakov preparing the way for Israel in exile, who are able to repair every place they reach. He links it to Motza'ei Shabbat, the way Rav Tzadok links the os to Shabbat.
ורמזו במדרש מחרן אנחנו. מחרונו של מקום כו' הידעתם שעתיד ללבן כו' ע"ש. ובגלות צריכין להתחזק ולהאמין כי הקב"ה עוזר לנו

**[Isaiah 1:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.1.18)** — אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ — If your sins be like scarlet, they shall become white as snow. The verse returns in ¶3 and ¶4. *Mafteach: found*

**[Shabbat 89b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.89b.2)** — ״כַּשָּׁנִים״? ״כַּשָּׁנִי״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ! ... אִם יִהְיוּ חֲטָאֵיכֶם כַּשָּׁנִים הַלָּלוּ שֶׁסְּדוּרוֹת וּבָאוֹת מִשֵּׁשֶׁת יְמֵי בְּרֵאשִׁית וְעַד עַכְשָׁיו — כַּשֶּׁלֶג יַלְבִּינוּ — The verse should say "like scarlet" (kashani); it says kashanim, "like the years": sins as many as the years that have run since Creation will become white as snow. Rav Tzadok ties "the six days of Creation" to the utterance "Bereishit," where every soul is rooted. *Mafteach: found*

**[Yoma 86b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.86b.3)** — גְּדוֹלָה תְּשׁוּבָה שֶׁזְּדוֹנוֹת נַעֲשׂוֹת לוֹ כִּזְכִיּוֹת ... כָּאן מֵאַהֲבָה, כָּאן מִיִּרְאָה — Great is teshuvah, for intentional sins become merits for him; this is teshuvah out of love. Just before this the same sugya cites our haftarah's verse, שׁוּבָה יִשְׂרָאֵל. *Mafteach: found*

**[Hosea 14:6–8](https://www.sefaria.org/Hosea.14.6-8)** — אֶהְיֶה כַטַּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל יִפְרַח כַּשּׁוֹשַׁנָּה וְיַךְ שָׁרָשָׁיו כַּלְּבָנוֹן ... וְרֵיחַ לוֹ כַּלְּבָנוֹן ... זִכְרוֹ כְּיֵין לְבָנוֹן — I will be like dew to Israel; he will blossom like the rose and strike his roots like Levanon... his fragrance like Levanon... his remembrance like the wine of Levanon. These are the three mentions of Levanon in the haftarah that ¶2 takes one by one. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar II 61b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Beshalach.28)** (Beshalach) — כָּל יוֹמָא וְיוֹמָא, נָטִיף טַלָּא מֵעַתִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא לִזְעֵיר אַפִּין, וּמִתְבָּרְכָאן כָּל חֲקַל תַּפּוּחִין קַדִּישִׁין — Every day dew drips from the Holy Ancient One to Ze'ir Anpin, and the whole field of holy apples is blessed. Rav Tzadok does not name a source; this is one place where the Zohar speaks of the dew of Atika. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Rosh Hashanah 32a](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.32a.19)** — ״וַיֹּאמֶר״ דִּבְרֵאשִׁית תִּשְׁעָה הָווּ! ״בְּרֵאשִׁית״ נָמֵי מַאֲמָר הוּא, דִּכְתִיב: ״בִּדְבַר ה׳ שָׁמַיִם נַעֲשׂוּ״ — There are only nine "And He said"s in the Creation story; "Bereishit" is also an utterance, as it says, "By the word of Hashem the heavens were made." The same words are in Megillah 21b. Rav Tzadok explains why this utterance has no "And He said": it is the hidden intellect. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Rashi on Genesis 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Genesis.1.1.2)** — בִּשְׁבִיל הַתּוֹרָה שֶׁנִקְרֵאת רֵאשִׁית דַּרְכּוֹ, וּבִשְׁבִיל יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִקְרְאוּ רֵאשִׁית תְּבוּאָתוֹ — For the sake of the Torah, called "the beginning of His way," and for the sake of Israel, called "the first of His crop." Rashi's derash, from the Midrash. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar I 1a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Introduction.1)** (Introduction) — כְּתִיב כְּשׁוֹשַׁנָּה בֵּין הַחוֹחִים. מָאן שׁוֹשַׁנָּה, דָּא כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל — "Like a rose among the thorns": who is the rose? This is Knesset Yisrael. The opening lines of the Zohar. *Mafteach: found*

**[Yoma 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.39b.7)** — אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן טַבְלַאי: לָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ לְבָנוֹן — שֶׁמַּלְבִּין עֲוֹנוֹתֵיהֶן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל — Why is [the Temple] called Levanon? Because it whitens the sins of Israel. This is the key to the os: Levanon, Lavan and "white as snow" are one theme. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Hosea 14:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Hosea.14.7)** — יֵלְכוּ יֹנְקוֹתָיו וִיהִי כַזַּיִת הוֹדוֹ וְרֵיחַ לוֹ כַּלְּבָנוֹן — His branches shall spread, his beauty shall be like the olive tree, and his fragrance like Levanon. The second Levanon. *Mafteach: found*

**[Eruvin 21b](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.21b.2)** — תְּאֵנִים הָרָעוֹת — אֵלּוּ רְשָׁעִים גְּמוּרִים. וְשֶׁמָּא תֹּאמַר אָבַד סִבְרָם וּבָטַל סִיכּוּיָם? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״הַדּוּדָאִים נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ״ — אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ עֲתִידִין שֶׁיִּתְּנוּ רֵיחַ — The bad figs are the completely wicked. Lest you think their hope is lost, the verse says "the dudaim give off fragrance": both these and those will give off fragrance. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Song of Songs 7:14](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs.7.14)** — הַדּוּדָאִים נָתְנוּ רֵיחַ וְעַל פְּתָחֵינוּ כָּל מְגָדִים — The mandrakes give off fragrance, and at our doors are all choice fruits. The Gemara reads דּוּדָאִים as two baskets (דּוּדֵי) of figs. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Vayeilech and Shabbat Shuvah 10](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Vayeilech_and_Shabbat_Shuvah_10) (Rav Tzadok) — the same chain on the same haftarah: Eruvin 21b (even the wicked will give off fragrance), Targum Yonatan's incense, galbanum and the sinners of Israel (Keritot 6b), Yoma 39b on Levanon, Shabbat 89b, and "Bereishit" as the hidden utterance. It adds the debate with the Maharsha on Yoma 86b (do sins themselves become merits?) and calls this level the fiftieth gate, open only to the ba'al teshuvah. *checked*

**[Jeremiah 24:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jeremiah.24.2)** — הַדּוּד אֶחָד תְּאֵנִים טֹבוֹת מְאֹד ... וְהַדּוּד אֶחָד תְּאֵנִים רָעוֹת מְאֹד — One basket of very good figs... and one basket of very bad figs. The verse behind the Gemara's "bad figs." *Mafteach: missing*

**[Rashi on Hosea 14:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Hosea.14.7)** and **[Targum Jonathan on Hosea 14:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Targum_Jonathan_on_Hosea.14.7)** — Rashi: ״יִסְגּוֹן בְּנִין וּבְנָן, וִיהִי כְּזִיו מְנָרְתָא דְקוּדְשָׁא זִיוְהוֹן וְרֵיחֲהוֹן כְּרֵיחַ קְטֹרֶת בּוּסְמַיָּא״; כַּלְּבָנוֹן — כְּבֵית מַקְדְּשָׁא — They will multiply sons and daughters, their radiance like the holy Menorah and their fragrance like the incense of spices; "like Levanon" means like the Temple. Rashi quotes the Targum verbatim. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Keritot 6b](https://www.sefaria.org/Keritot.6b.18)** — כׇּל תַּעֲנִית שֶׁאֵין בָּהּ מִפּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָהּ תַּעֲנִית, שֶׁהֲרֵי חֶלְבְּנָה רֵיחָהּ רַע וּמְנָאָהּ הַכָּתוּב עִם סַמְמָנֵי קְטֹרֶת — A fast that does not include the sinners of Israel is no fast, for galbanum smells bad, yet Scripture listed it with the incense spices. The Gemara reads עִם where Rav Tzadok has בֵּין, as in the Yalkut. Abaye adds וַאֲגֻדָּתוֹ עַל אֶרֶץ יְסָדָהּ, the "bundle" behind Rav Tzadok's כְּשֶׁהֵן בַּאֲגֻדָּה. *Mafteach: found*

**[Hosea 14:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Hosea.14.8)** — יָשֻׁבוּ יֹשְׁבֵי בְצִלּוֹ יְחַיּוּ דָגָן וְיִפְרְחוּ כַגָּפֶן זִכְרוֹ כְּיֵין לְבָנוֹן — Those who dwell in his shade shall return; they shall revive like grain and blossom like the vine; his remembrance like the wine of Levanon. The third Levanon. The Mafteach lists Hosea 14:6 (with 14:7) but not this verse. *Mafteach: missing*

notes.anchor: (פְּסָחִים קו עַמּוּד א, דִּבּוּר הַמַּתְחִיל זוֹכְרֵהוּ)
notes.text: **[Tosafot on Pesachim 106a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tosafot_on_Pesachim.106a)** (s.v. זוכרהו על היין) — דזכירה כתיב על היין זכרו כיין לבנון (הושע י״ד:ח׳) נזכירה דודיך מיין (שיר השירים א׳:ד׳) והאי זכירה היינו קידוש — "Remembrance" is written of wine, "his remembrance like the wine of Levanon," "we will remember Your love more than wine," and this remembrance is Kiddush. *Mafteach: found*

**[Song of Songs 1:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs.1.4)** — משכני אחריך נרוצה ... נגילה ונשמחה בך נזכירה דדיך מיין מישרים אהבוך — Draw me after You and we will run... we will rejoice in You, we will remember Your love more than wine. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Targum Jonathan on Hosea 14:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Targum_Jonathan_on_Hosea.14.8)** — יְהֵי דָכְרָן טַבְוָתְהוֹן עָלֵיל וְלָא פָסֵיק ... עַל חֲמַר עַתִּיק דְמִתְנַסֵךְ בְּבֵית מַקְדָשָׁא — The remembrance of their good deeds will rise and never cease, like... the old wine that is poured as a libation in the Temple. Rav Tzadok takes "the wine of Levanon" as the Temple's libation wine. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar II 92b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Yitro.33)** (Yitro) — זָכוֹר, אֲתָר דְּלֵית לֵיהּ שִׁכְחָה, וְלָא קַיְּימָא בֵּיהּ שִׁכְחָה — "Zachor": a place that has no forgetting, where no forgetting abides. The Zohar is speaking of זָכוֹר אֶת יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת and of Kiddush, the same Kiddush that Tosafot learn from "his remembrance like the wine of Levanon." *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 162b–163a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.37)** (Vayetzei) — תָּא חֲזֵי יִשְׂבְּעוּ עֲצֵי ה' אַרְזֵי לְבָנוֹן אֲשֶׁר נָטָע. מַאן לְבָנוֹן. הָא אוּקְמוּהָ ... אֲשֶׁר שָׁם צִפֳּרִים יְקַנֵּנוּ, בְּאָן אֲתַר, בַּלְּבָנוֹן. וְאִלֵּין אִינוּן תְּרֵין צִפֳּרִים ... אֲבָל אִלֵּין עִלָּאִין וְנָפְקִין מִלְּבָנוֹן דְּאִיהוּ לְעֵילָא, וְרָזָא דְמִלָּה, וּלְלָבָן שְׁתֵּי בָנוֹת — What is Levanon? It has been explained... "where birds nest": in Levanon. These are the two birds... supernal ones that issue from Levanon, which is above, and the secret is "Lavan had two daughters." The passage begins at the foot of 162b and runs onto 163a, as Rav Tzadok says. Its printed text reads אוּקְמוּהָ. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Psalms 104:16–17](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.104.16-17)** — יִשְׂבְּעוּ עֲצֵי ה' אַרְזֵי לְבָנוֹן אֲשֶׁר נָטָע. אֲשֶׁר שָׁם צִפֳּרִים יְקַנֵּנוּ חֲסִידָה בְּרוֹשִׁים בֵּיתָהּ — The trees of Hashem are sated, the cedars of Levanon that He planted, where birds make their nests; the stork, the cypresses are her house. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar II 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Shemot.3)** (Shemot) — אִתִּי מִלְּבָנוֹן כַּלָּה, קוֹל אֲמַר לְדִבּוּר אִתִּי, בְּגִין דְּהָא קוֹל אָתֵי לְדִבּוּר ... דְּהָא לֵית קוֹל בְּלֹא דִּבּוּר, וְלֵית דִּבּוּר בְּלא קוֹל. וְעַל דָּא אִתִּי מִלְּבָנוֹן כַּלָּה וְגוֹ', דְּעִקָרָא דְּתַרְוַיְיהוּ מִלְּבָנוֹן קָא אַתְיָין — R. Shimon: "With me from Levanon, O bride" is voice saying to speech "with me"; there is no voice without speech and no speech without voice, and the root of both comes from Levanon. The passage begins on 2b and R. Shimon's words are on 3a. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Song of Songs 4:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Song_of_Songs.4.8)** — אתי מלבנון כלה אתי מלבנון תבואי תשורי מראש אמנה — With me from Levanon, O bride, with me from Levanon you shall come; look from the peak of Amanah. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar III 2a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayikra.1)** (Vayikra) with **[Joshua 2:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Joshua.2.12)** — וְכֵן בְּרָחָב מַה כְּתִיב, וּנְתַתֶּם לִי אוֹת אֱמֶת, דָּא אָת ו', דְּדָא אִקְרֵי אוֹת אֱמֶת — Of Rachav it says "give me a true sign": this is the letter Vav, which is called "the true sign." The verse: ונתתם לי אות אמת. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Sulam on Zohar, Vayetzei 337](https://www.sefaria.org/Sulam_on_Zohar,_Vayetzei.337)** (Kabbalah) — the Sulam explains the same Zohar: Levanon is Binah returned to Chochmah (ל"ב paths of wisdom and the נ' gates of understanding), the two birds are Leah and Rachel, and Lavan is Levanon. Rav Tzadok makes Levanon Da'at, the inwardness of Keter, but reads the two daughters as the two "worlds" in the same way.
ואלו הם ב' צפרים שבארנו בכמה מקומות, דהיינו ב' נוקבין דז"א, לאה ורחל

**[Genesis 29:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.29.16)** — וּלְלָבָן שְׁתֵּי בָנוֹת שֵׁם הַגְּדֹלָה לֵאָה וְשֵׁם הַקְּטַנָּה רָחֵל — Lavan had two daughters; the elder was named Leah and the younger Rachel. *Mafteach: missing*

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Divrei Emet, Divrei Emet on Torah, Vayetzei 5](https://www.sefaria.org/Divrei_Emet,_Divrei_Emet_on_Torah,_Vayetzei.5)** (Chassidus) — the Chozeh of Lublin also reads "Lavan" here as the supernal whiteness, with the two daughters as the two ways to reach it. He makes Rachel the root of Knesset Yisrael, as Rav Tzadok does.
דהנה פירשנו על וללבן שתי בנות כו'. פי' הלובן עליון הקדושה והבהירות שתי ענינים מקבלים משם
sefaria: Divrei Emet, Divrei Emet on Torah, Vayetzei 5

notes.text: **[Rashi on Leviticus 1:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Leviticus.1.1)** (from the Sifra) — וּמֶה הָיוּ הַפְסָקוֹת מְשַׁמְּשׁוֹת? לִתֵּן רֶוַח לְמֹשֶׁה לְהִתְבּוֹנֵן בֵּין פָּרָשָׁה לְפָרָשָׁה וּבֵין עִנְיָן לְעִנְיָן — What were the breaks for? To give Moshe a pause to reflect between one section and the next. Parashat Vayetzei has no open or closed section break at all, so it is all one subject. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar I 163a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.38)** (Vayetzei) — אִם חָכַמְתָּ חָכַמְתָּ לָךְ ... דְּהָא כָּל מִילֵי דְאוֹרַיְיתָא, כֻּלְּהוּ מִלִּין עִלָּאִין וְיַקִּירִין. וְכָל מִלָּה וּמִלָּה כְּתִיב בָּהּ יְקָרָה הִיא מִפְּנִינִים — R. Elazar: woe to those who see the words of the Torah as empty; all its words are supernal and precious, and of each one it says "more precious than pearls." He says it on Yaakov's rods (Genesis 30:38), right inside the "stories" of this parashah. The Zohar text reads יְקָרָה without the vav. *Mafteach: found*

**[Proverbs 9:12](https://www.sefaria.org/Proverbs.9.12)** — אִם חָכַמְתָּ חָכַמְתָּ לָּךְ וְלַצְתָּ לְבַדְּךָ תִשָּׂא — If you are wise, you are wise for yourself; if you scoff, you alone will bear it. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Proverbs 3:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Proverbs.3.15)** — יקרה היא מפנינים וכל חפציך לא ישוו בה — It is more precious than pearls, and all your desires cannot equal it. Neither the verse nor the Zohar has the vav that the print has (see the editor's note). *Mafteach: found*

**[Berakhot 17a](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.17a.2)** — רִבּוֹן הָעוֹלָמִים, גָּלוּי וְיָדוּעַ לְפָנֶיךָ שֶׁרְצוֹנֵנוּ לַעֲשׂוֹת רְצוֹנֶךָ, וּמִי מְעַכֵּב? — שְׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה וְשִׁעְבּוּד מַלְכֻיוֹת — Master of the world, it is revealed before You that our will is to do Your will; what holds us back? The yeast in the dough and the subjugation to the kingdoms. R. Alexandri's prayer: at the root Israel's will is one with God's, and only the evil inclination and exile hold it back. *Mafteach: found*

**[Isaiah 60:21](https://www.sefaria.org/Isaiah.60.21)** — וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים לְעוֹלָם יִירְשׁוּ אָרֶץ נֵצֶר מַטָּעַי מַעֲשֵׂה יָדַי לְהִתְפָּאֵר — Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of My planting, the work of My hands. Yosef, the tzaddik, completes the repair of what all Israel do. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 163a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.37)** (Vayetzei) — חֲסִידָה בְּרוֹשִׁים בֵּיתָהּ, בְּאִינוּן שִׁית בְּנִין עִלָּאִין, שִׁית סִטְרִין דְּעָלְמָא ... הַאי עַלְמָא עִלָּאָה אַף עַל גַּב דְּנוּקְבָא אִיהִי, קָרִינָן לָהּ דָּכָר — "The stork, the cypresses are her house": in the six supernal children, the six sides of the world; this upper world, though female, is called male. The same Zohar passage as [3.1], continued. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Bereshit Rabbah 73:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.73.11)** — רַבִּי לֵוִי אָמַר שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא כְּלָבִים ... מַאן דַּאֲמַר שִׁשִּׁים רִבּוֹא, לְכָל עֵדֶר וְעֵדֶר חַד כֶּלֶב — R. Levi: [Yaakov had] six hundred thousand dogs, one dog for each flock. So he had 600,000 flocks. On וַיִּפְרֹץ הָאִישׁ (Genesis 30:43). *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Pesach Sheni 2](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Pesach_Sheni_2) (Rav Tzadok) — "it is known that the Torah has 600,000 letters and against them are 600,000 souls of Israel, and every soul has a share in the letters of the Torah." Pesach Sheni then becomes the sign that no soul is lost, even one who was far away on purpose, and it ends with the same Shabbat 89b "if your sins be like the years." *checked*

**[Genesis 30:40](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.30.40)** — וְהַכְּשָׂבִים הִפְרִיד יַעֲקֹב ... וַיָּשֶׁת לוֹ עֲדָרִים לְבַדּוֹ וְלֹא שָׁתָם עַל צֹאן לָבָן — Yaakov separated the lambs... and he set his own flocks apart and did not put them with Lavan's flock. *Mafteach: found*

**[Zohar I 163b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.38)** (Vayetzei) — וְלֹא שָׁתָם עַל צֹאן לָבָן, דְּלָא שַׁוֵּי חוּלָקֵיהּ וְעַדְבֵיהּ עִמְּהוֹן — "He did not put them with Lavan's flock": he did not set his portion and lot with them. The same section also says Yaakov בָּרִיר לֵיהּ סִטְרָא דִימִינָא, "sifted out the right side", which is Rav Tzadok's שֶׁבֵּירֵר. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar I 162a–b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.32)** (Vayetzei, Sitrei Torah) — וישת לו עדרים לבדו ולא שתם על צאן לבן. (אינון) עדרים אפריש ליה לגרמיה, דלא יהא ליה חולק בשאר עממין — He set apart flocks for himself, so that he would have no share with the other nations. The Sitrei Torah section begins on 162a; these words run from the foot of 162a onto 162b. *Mafteach: missing*
**[Psalms 92:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.92.2)** — טוב להדות לה' ולזמר לשמך עליון — It is good to give thanks to Hashem and to sing to Your name, Most High. *Mafteach: found*

**[Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer 19](https://www.sefaria.org/Pirkei_DeRabbi_Eliezer.19)** — ״טוֹב לְהֹדוֹת לַה'״. אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן אָמַר: בִּי יִלְמְדוּ כָּל הַדּוֹרוֹת שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁיּוֹדֶה פְּשָׁעָיו וְעוֹזֵב נִיצּוֹל מִדִּינָהּ שֶׁל גֵּיהִנֹּם — Adam said: from me all generations will learn that whoever confesses his sins and forsakes them is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom. The same chapter reads "like a cedar in Levanon" (Psalms 92:13). Midrash Tehillim 92:5 has nearly the same words. PRE does not cite Proverbs 28:13; Rav Tzadok adds it. *Mafteach: wrong label (index: Shocher Tov [Midrash Tehillim] 52:4)*

**[Proverbs 28:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Proverbs.28.13)** — מְכַסֶּה פְשָׁעָיו לֹא יַצְלִיחַ וּמוֹדֶה וְעֹזֵב יְרֻחָם — One who conceals his sins will not succeed; one who confesses and forsakes them will obtain mercy. *Mafteach: found*

**[Psalms 92:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Psalms.92.13)** — צדיק כתמר יפרח כארז בלבנון ישגה — The righteous will flourish like a palm tree; he will grow tall like a cedar in Levanon. So the Shabbat psalm opens with confession and closes with Levanon, the whitening of sin. *Mafteach: found*

**Parallels:** [Peri Tzadik, Metzora 4](#/read/Peri_Tzadik,_Metzora_4) (Rav Tzadok) — reads the same verse of the Shabbat psalm with Yoma 39b: the Temple is Levanon because it whitens sins, and its incense repairs the galbanum, the sinners of Israel. It adds that "Levanon" is ל"ב and נ', Chochmah and Binah, and that the cedar rooted there is Da'at, which grows "without measure" up to Atik. *checked*

**[Deuteronomy 1:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.1.11)** — ה' אֱלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵכֶם יֹסֵף עֲלֵיכֶם כָּכֶם אֶלֶף פְּעָמִים וִיבָרֵךְ אֶתְכֶם כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָכֶם — May Hashem, the God of your fathers, add to you a thousand times like yourselves, and bless you as He has spoken to you. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Rashi on Deuteronomy 1:11](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Deuteronomy.1.11)** and **[Devarim Rabbah 1:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Devarim_Rabbah.1.13)** — Rashi: אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מֹשֶׁה אַתָּה נוֹתֵן קִצְבָּה לְבִרְכוֹתֵינוּ? ... אָמַר לָהֶם זוֹ מִשֶּׁלִּי הִיא, אֲבָל הוּא יְבָרֵךְ אֶתְכֶם כַּאֲשֶׁר דִּבֶּר לָכֶם (from the Sifrei). The Midrash: הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לֹא נָתַן קִצְּבָה לְבִרְכוֹתֵינוּ וְאַתָּה אָמַרְתָּ אֶלֶף פְּעָמִים, אָמַר לָהֶם מַה שֶּׁבֵּרַכְתִי אֶתְכֶם מִשֶּׁלִּי בֵּרַכְתִּי — "Moshe, are you setting a limit to our blessings?" "This one is mine; He will bless you as He has spoken." The Midrash also explains that God's "addition" is greater than the principal. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Zohar I 161a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zohar,_Vayetzei.30)** (Vayetzei) — רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר, אֶלֶף עָאנִין, וְאֶלֶף אִמְרִין, וְאֶלֶף עִזִּין, הֲוָה מַיְיתֵי לֵיהּ יַעֲקֹב יַתִּיר בְּכָל יַרְחָא וְיַרְחָא ... וּבִרְכְתָא דִלְעֵילָא לָאו אִיהוּ פָּחוֹת מֵאֶלֶף מִכָּל זִינָא וְזִינָא — R. Abba: Yaakov brought Lavan an extra thousand sheep, a thousand lambs and a thousand goats every month, for blessing from above is never less than a thousand of each kind. The Zohar reads הֲוָה מַיְיתֵי and לָאו where the print has הווּ and לָא. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Genesis 30:30](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.30.30)** — כִּי מְעַט אֲשֶׁר הָיָה לְךָ לְפָנַי וַיִּפְרֹץ לָרֹב וַיְבָרֶךְ ה' אֹתְךָ לְרַגְלִי — For the little you had before me has grown abundantly, and Hashem has blessed you on my account. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Sefer Yetzirah 1:7](https://www.sefaria.org/Sefer_Yetzirah.1.7)** — עשר ספירות בלי מה ... שאדון יחיד ואין לו שני ולפני אחד מה אתה סופר — Ten sefirot of nothingness... for the Master is unique and has no second, and before One, what do you count? In Atzilut there is nothing yet to count, so the blessing is "units." *Mafteach: missing*

**[Genesis 2:3](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.2.3)** — וַיְבָרֶךְ אֱלֹהִים אֶת יוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי וַיְקַדֵּשׁ אֹתוֹ כִּי בוֹ שָׁבַת מִכׇּל מְלַאכְתּוֹ — God blessed the seventh day and made it holy, for on it He rested from all His work. *Mafteach: missing*

**[Sha'ar HaKavanot, Sermons on the Order of the Sabbath 1:4](https://www.sefaria.org/Sha'ar_HaKavanot,_Sermons_on_the_Order_of_the_Sabbath.1.4)** — ומתעכבים באדם שלשתם ביום א מהשבוע וליל ב מסתלקת הנשמה ונשארים נפש ורוח ובליל שלישי מסתלקת הרוח ובליל ד מסתלקת גם הנפש ואחר כך צריך עוד לעשות תיקון מחדש ולקבל תוספת שלשתם בשלשה ימים הנשארים — The added Neshamah, Ruach and Nefesh all stay through Sunday; on the night that begins Monday the Neshamah leaves, on the night that begins Tuesday the Ruach, and on the night that begins Wednesday the Nefesh. On the three days left one must receive all three again for the coming Shabbat.  This is the source of Rav Tzadok's order: Neshamah-Ruach-Nefesh after Shabbat, Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah before it. *Mafteach: missing*
sefaria: Sha'ar HaKavanot, Sermons on the Order of the Sabbath 1:4

notes.text:
**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Bat Ayin, Beha'alotcha 18](https://www.sefaria.org/Bat_Ayin,_Beha'alotcha.18)** (Chassidus) — R. Avraham Dov of Avritch states the same order exactly: before Shabbat the flow comes as Nefesh, Ruach, Neshamah, and after Shabbat in reverse, Neshamah, Ruach, Nefesh. He finds it in the inverted nuns around וַיְהִי בִּנְסֹעַ.
היינו שקודם השבת נמשך בזה הסדר נפש רוח נשמה ... והמשכת השפע שלאחר השבת הוא בזה הסדר, נשמה רוח נפש

**Parallels beyond the library:** **[Sidduro Shel Shabbat, Volume II, Derush II 2:18](https://www.sefaria.org/Sidduro_Shel_Shabbat,_Volume_II,_Derush_II.2.18)** (Chassidus) — cites the same teaching of the Ari: the three days before Shabbat belong to it as preparation, and Shabbat then shines into the three days after it. He describes Shabbat as standing in the middle, both receiving and giving, while Rav Tzadok counts the flow by worlds.
כאשר ידוע מכתבי האר"י ששלשה ימים קודם השבת המה שייכים להשבת ... ואח"כ היא מאירה ומשפיע אורה בשלשה ימים אחר השבת

notes.text: **[Tikkunei Zohar 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Tikkunei_Zohar.23a)** (Tikkun 6) — וכן מטטרו"ן אוליף זכו על עופין דיליה דאינון רוחין דפרחין בבני נשא. דמכרסיא אינון נשמתין. ומהאי חיה רוחין. ומאופן נפשין. ואינון בבריאה יצירה עשייה — Metatron pleads for his birds, the spirits that fly among people: from the Throne come the neshamot, from the Chayah the ruchot, from the Ofan the nefashot, and they are in Beriah, Yetzirah, Asiyah. This is part of Tikkun 6, on the mitzvah of sending away the mother bird. *Mafteach: found*

connector.why: Same haftarah, same chain: Eruvin 21b, Targum Yonatan's incense, galbanum (Keritot 6b), Yoma 39b, Shabbat 89b, Bereishit as the hidden utterance. Adds the Maharsha on Yoma 86b and the fiftieth gate.
Psalms 92:13 with Yoma 39b; the Temple as Levanon that whitens sin; incense repairing the galbanum; Levanon = Chochmah/Binah; the cedar = Da'at up to Atik.
Paragraph 1 (read) is on the three Shabbat meals and the Ari's zemirot; the shared sources (BR 70:10, Yoma 39b) are in a later paragraph that was not read, so no note.
600,000 letters of the Torah = 600,000 souls; no soul is lost; ends with Shabbat 89b 'like the years'.

candidates.why: Commentary on Rav Tzadok's own Zohar (162b-163a): Levanon = Binah returned to Chochmah, two birds = Leah and Rachel, Lavan = Levanon.
This is the Zohar passage Rav Tzadok himself quotes in ¶3, so it is a source, not a parallel; it has its own source note.

Lurianic gloss setting kelipah counterparts against the two birds and Lavan's two daughters; it touches 'under Lavan's hand, in the kelipah' but does not develop Rav Tzadok's idea. Sefaria also refused this ref.
A plain-sense discussion of the seven years and the switch of Leah for Rachel; it shares only the words of the verses.

found.why: Uses BR 70:10 ('who will whiten your sins') to read Lavan as a supernal attribute, not as the villain.
BR 70:10 'from Charan... who will whiten' as Yaakov preparing Israel's repair in exile; linked to Shabbat and Motza'ei Shabbat.
Same order: Nefesh-Ruach-Neshamah before Shabbat, Neshamah-Ruach-Nefesh after.
